issue.title: sase agent wait --for-epic/--no-for-epic: follow a planner into the epic it launches from the shell
issue.description:
Proposed by sase-1h7.10 note #2 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP), triaged by the sase-1h7 land agent.
Explicitly listed as out of scope in plan 202610/wait_for_epic.md ("Out of Scope", research Q2).

`%wait` now follows a target into every epic it launches by default (`for_epic=true`), with a
per-occurrence `for_epic=false` opt-out. The shell-side `sase agent wait NAME...` command
("Block until the agents you name ... reach a terminal state") still returns as soon as a
planner finishes, even when that planner just launched an epic. Scripts like
`sase agent wait planner && just check-full` therefore race the epic's phases.

Proposal: add `--for-epic/--no-for-epic` to `sase agent wait`, reusing the shared
epic-follow decision (`sase.core.wait_dependency_resolution.resolve_wait_release` and the
sase-core `wait_epic_follow_reduce` reducer) so the CLI, `%wait`, and the TUI agree. Decide
the CLI default (the research recommended matching `%wait`'s default), how the JSON envelope
reports followed epics (reuse `describe_epic_follow` phrasing and the `epic_follows` shape
from `sase agent list -j`), and how exit codes treat a BLOCKED follow (likely exit 3,
"blocked on a human").

task_type_fields.proposal: Add --for-epic/--no-for-epic to sase agent wait, reusing the shared epic-follow release decision so the CLI, %wait, and TUI agree on when a planner-plus-epic wait settles, including JSON envelope and exit-code semantics for following/blocked states.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Plan 202610/wait_for_epic.md lists sase agent wait --for-epic/--no-for-epic (research Q2) under Out of Scope; sase-1h7.10 recorded it as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP.

issue.creation_reason: The %wait directive now follows targets into launched epics by default, but the shell sase agent wait still releases at planner completion; the epic plan deferred CLI parity as research Q2.
